title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space and defense sectors are experiencing a mix of strategic shifts and funding boosts as governments and companies alike scramble to enhance capabilities. With significant investments flowing into satellite technology and defense strategies, the landscape is evolving rapidly, albeit with some hiccups in hypersonic testing.

themes.title: Funding Floodgates Open
themes.body: Flexell Space's recent $20 million Series A round and True Anomaly's $190 million Series C demonstrate the growing investor appetite for space startups. Meanwhile, the U.K. government's forthcoming space strategy hints at a broader commitment to bolstering its own space economy.

themes.title: Defense Spending Surge
themes.body: Europe's space economy is buoyed by increased defense spending, with the FY27 budget markup adding $1.4 billion to space resilience initiatives. This financial injection is likely to catalyze further collaboration between government and private sectors.

themes.title: Satellite Expansion Plans
themes.body: L3Harris and Sierra Space are set to enhance the U.S. missile-tracking network with 36 new satellites, while Anduril and L3Harris are teaming up for a tactical satellite constellation bid. These moves underscore the escalating competition in the satellite domain.

themes.title: Hypersonic Hurdles Persist
themes.body: The hypersonic glide-vehicle test has once again slipped, marking the third consecutive quarter of delays. This raises questions about the reliability of timelines in a field where speed is of the essence.
